title: Fauci Pleads the Fifth
hook: “Nothing says honesty like taking the Fifth, huh, Doc?”
desc: Sen. Josh Hawley grills Dr. Fauci in a Senate hearing — asking what day of the week it is, what color tie he's wearing — and gets the Fifth Amendment every time. 111 invocations, zero answers.
tags: Josh Hawley Fauci Fifth Amendment Senate hearing US politics
text: Well, nothing says honesty like taking the fifth, and Doc, let's try something. What day of the week is it today? On the advice of counsel, I respectfully decline to answer based upon my rights under the Fifth Amendment to the Constitution. Oh, color tie you're wearing. On the advice of counsel, I respectfully decline to answer based upon my rights under the Fifth Amendment to the Constitution. What color is the carpet in front of you? On the advice of counsel, I respectfully decline to answer based upon my rights under the Fifth Amendment to the Constitution. Let's just get one thing straight. You don't have any rights under the Fifth Amendment because you've been pardoned, as you very well know, as a Supreme Court has been clear for a century and more, Brown versus Walker, 1896. When he has been pardoned, he may not stand upon his privilege. You know that, your lawyers sitting behind you now shifting nervously in their chairs, they know it. This isn't about the Constitution, this isn't about the law, this is about contempt. For this body and contempt for the American people. But I think I know why you're doing it. It's because you don't want to answer questions. It's because you did all kinds of terrible things. It's because during the pandemic, you got rich, didn't you? You got rich while people were dying, hundreds of thousands of Americans over a million in the end and you were getting rich and not only were you doing that, you were using federal employees with taxpayer money to apply for and solicit cash prizes for you personally, cash prizes totaling over a million dollars. You did all of that during the pandemic, didn't you? That's a question. On the advice of counsel, I respectfully decline to answer based upon my rights under the Fifth Amendment to the Constitution.

title: Hawley Grills Fauci on 111 Fifth Amendment Invocations
hook: “He looked very carefully at the carpet.”
desc: Sen. Hawley explains why he asked Dr. Fauci about his tie and the carpet: to test the good faith of 111 Fifth Amendment invocations — including questions with no fear of prosecution. “That is an abuse… there's no privilege for any of that.”
tags: Josh Hawley Fauci Fifth Amendment Senate hearing US politics
text: The reason that I asked Dr. Fauci what color his tie was and what day of the week it was and what color the carpet is. What color is the carpet in front of you? He looked by the way. I thought he was going to answer that one. He looked very carefully at the carpet. The reason I asked those questions was precisely to test the good faith nature of his invocation at the Fifth Amendment. I think it's pretty clear given Dr. Fauci's 111 invocations of the Fifth Amendment included questions that he had could have no fear of prosecution on. It's going to get prosecuted for the color of his tie. It shows that he had no interest and no intention of answering any of our questions and that is an abuse of the pro that there's no privilege for any of that.

title: France Student Protests: Tear Gas in Paris as Hundreds of Thousands March
hook: “They don't really care about us” — students, teachers and parents flood the streets of Paris.
desc: France's student protest wave peaks on October 6 with a national day of demonstrations: 256,000 marchers counted by the Interior Ministry, 450,000 by organizers, up to 100,000 in Paris marching from République to Nation. What began September 21 at a Créteil high school over teacher shortages, overcrowded classes and crumbling buildings has spread nationwide — 24 schools burned or ransacked, 78 staff injured, over 6,500 arrested, mostly minors. Police fired tear gas as the Paris march ended; Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu suspended classes through the week.
tags: France student protests Paris tear gas education Macron
